name: Percutaneous nasal osteotomy

card.summary: Percutaneous nasal osteotomy is a rhinoplasty technique that breaks and repositions the nasal bones through tiny skin stabs, used to narrow a wide nasal bridge or straighten the nose.
card.note: Surgery under anaesthesia; swelling can take at least a year to settle.

quick.overview:
Percutaneous (external) osteotomy cuts the nasal bones through tiny stab incisions in the skin rather than from inside the nose. It is used in rhinoplasty to realign bones, close an open roof after hump reduction or narrow the nose.
The visible result is a narrower or straighter nasal bridge. It is a surgical procedure done by a surgeon.
quick.how: Patients consult a rhinoplasty surgeon, who chooses the osteotomy approach as part of the plan. After surgery the nose is taped and splinted, with the dressing typically removed after about one week.
quick.risks: Risks of rhinoplasty include deformities such as open roof, saddle nose and rocker deformity. Swelling can take a year or more to subside, and smoking can compromise healing.

lead: An osteotomy is a surgical operation in which a bone is cut to change its alignment.[2] In rhinoplasty, nasal bones are cut and repositioned to reduce a bony hump, narrow the nose or realign it.[1]

Percutaneous osteotomy is the approach that makes the cuts through very small skin stabs instead of from inside the nose, in contrast with internal (endonasal) approaches. Surgeons choose between techniques based on the case.

chain: Bones cut through small skin stabs
Nasal bones moved inward or straightened
angle.text: The procedure changes the width and alignment of the bony nasal bridge. Results are permanent surgical changes once healed.

infobox: Splint ~1 week; swelling up to a year+[1]

paras: Rhinoplasty can reduce bony humps and realign the nasal bones after they are cut, and may also improve breathing.[1] Piezoelectric ultrasonic instruments are an alternative that affect only bone and stiff cartilage.[1]

The nose is taped and splinted, with dressings removed at about a week, and swelling can take at least a year to diminish.[1] Described deformities include pollybeak, saddle nose, inverted-V, rocker and open roof.[1]
No studies specific to this approach have been published.

timeline.event: John Orlando Roe performs the first modern endonasal rhinoplasty.[1]
Jacques Joseph describes nose-reduction rhinoplasty through internal incisions.[1]
